exposure: Residential greenspace (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index - NDVI, Enhanced Vegetation Index - EVI)
cohort: The study included 16,605 children aged 3-12 years residing in Shanghai, China.
finding: Higher individual-level exposure to residential greenspace was associated with decreased odds of asthma in children, with the association modified by ambient temperature and residential area.
cross-section timing: Asthma symptoms and covariates were collected in 2019, with residential greenspace data averaged from 2016 to 2018.
